title: RINGKASAN EKSEKUTIF PENGEMBANGAN PAKET R: fastsae
text: Dalam penyusunan kebijakan publik berbasis bukti (evidence-based policy), pemerintah membutuhkan indikator sosial-ekonomi (seperti persentase kemiskinan, prevalensi stunting, tingkat pengangguran) hingga tingkat wilayah administrasi yang sangat kecil (kabupaten/kota, kecamatan, bahkan desa/kelurahan). Namun, Badan Pusat Statistik (BPS) dan lembaga statistik resmi internasional menghadapi tiga kendala fundamental: 1. Keterbatasan Ukuran Sampel Survei: Penduga langsung (direct estimator) seperti survei Susenas/Sakernas memiliki ukuran sampel yang sangat kecil atau bahkan nol di level mikro, menghasilkan Relative Standard Error (RSE / CV) yang sangat tinggi (>30%) sehingga tidak reliabel untuk dipublikasikan. 2. Hambatan Komputasi Metode Bayesian (MCMC): Pendekatan Bayesian hierarkis selama ini mengandalkan algoritma Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC melalui Stan/JAGS). Pada skala nasional dengan ratusan kabupaten/kota atau ribuan desa, dan terutama pada pemodelan spasio-temporal, MCMC membutuhkan waktu komputasi yang sangat lambat (berkisar antara puluhan menit hingga berjam-jam) serta sering menghadapi masalah konvergensi rantai (chain convergence). 3. Ketiadaan Solusi Terpadu untuk Model Non-Gaussian & Kalibrasi Konsistensi: - Paket R SAE konvensional (misalnya paket sae dan emdi) sebagian besar mengasumsikan distribusi normal/Gaussian, yang sering menghasilkan estimasi tidak realistis (misalnya proporsi bernilai negatif atau >100%). - Angka estimasi area kecil sering kali tidak cocok jika dijumlahkan kembali ke angka agregat resmi nasional atau provinsi (inconsistency issue).

what: 2. Solusi & Kebaruan yang Ditawarkan Paket fastsae
title: RINGKASAN EKSEKUTIF PENGEMBANGAN PAKET R: fastsae
text: Paket fastsae dirancang sebagai ekosistem komputasi SAE modern yang menggabungkan kecepatan komputasi deterministik tinggi, fleksibilitas distribusi probabilitas, dan kepatuhan terhadap kaidah produksi statistik resmi: Akselerasi Berbasis INLA (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations): Mengganti simulasi MCMC dengan aproksimasi analitik Laplace bersarang dan aljabar matriks jarang (sparse matrix C++). Memberikan hasil posterior mean dan interval kredibel yang identik dengan MCMC, namun dengan kecepatan 10x hingga 100x lebih cepat (konvergensi dalam hitungan detik). Area-Level Gaussian: Model standar Fay-Herriot (FH), Spasial FH (SAR, CAR, BYM2), dan Spasio-Temporal FH (AR(1) temporal autoregressive dengan struktur interaksi ruang-waktu Knorr-Held). Non-Gaussian Hierarchical Bayes (HB): Model Beta (untuk indikator terbatas 0<θ<10 < \theta < 1 seperti proporsi kemiskinan), Binomial/Logit (prevalensi dengan denominator ukuran sampel), dan Poisson (frekuensi kejadian langka dengan offset populasi berisiko). Unit-Level Models: Model Battese-Harter-Fuller (BHF) dengan metode analitik cepat Henderson III dan REML. Inovasi Kalibrasi: Two-Stage Hierarchical Benchmarking (benchmark_sae): Memastikan estimasi level kabupaten/kota secara serentak konsisten dengan target provinsi, dan target provinsi konsisten dengan target nasional: ∑d∈Provgw̃dgθ̂dgBM=Tg*dan∑gW̃gTg*=Tnat\sum_{d \\text{Prov}_g} \tilde{w}_{dg} \hat{\theta}_{dg}^{\text{BM}} = T_g^* \quad \text{dan} \quad \sum_g \tilde{W}_g T_g^* = T_{\text{nat}} Mendukung metode Ratio, Difference, Optimal Variance-Weighted Quadratic Loss (Datta et al. 2011; Steorts et al. 2014), dan Constrained Logit (Berg & Fuller 2014). Perangkat Diagnostik & Standar Mutu Statistik Otomatis: Dilengkapi uji kalibrasi Brown et al. (2001) (uji regresi bias dan uji Wald WW), otomatisasi klasifikasi reliabilitas indikator (Reliable / Caution / Unreliable), komparasi model otomatis (compare_models), visualisasi peta tematik (map_sae), serta ekspor data multi-format ber-metadata (export_sae).

text: tipsae (Stan MCMC): ~420 detik (7 menit) dengan 4 chains x 2000 iterasi. fastsae (INLA): ~3.4 detik (akselerasi lebih dari 120x lebih cepat). title: Bayesian Area-Level Small Area Estimation with INLA
text: Classical Small Area Estimation (SAE) models—Fay-Herriot (1979) model—traditionally assume Gaussian distribution direct survey estimators known sampling error variances. However, real-world official statistics frequently encounter non-Gaussian indicators: - Poverty rates, unemployment rates, prevalence ratios: strictly bounded open interval (0,1)(0, 1). - Disease counts, crime incidents, rare events: discrete counts subject Poisson Negative Binomial overdispersion population exposures. - Binary survey aggregates: proportions derived small sample sizes (Binomial trials). - Skewed economic expenditures: strictly positive continuous outcomes (Gamma). Furthermore, data collected across geographical areas repeated time (panel/longitudinal surveys), outcomes exhibit spatial dependency temporal autocorrelation. fastsae package introduces hb_area(), unified hierarchical Bayesian framework powered Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA). provides fast, deterministic, highly accurate analytical posterior approximations without computational bottlenecks, convergence diagnostics, chain-tuning associated Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC).

title: Model Diagnostics and Residual Analysis
text: Small Area Estimation (SAE), model-based estimators borrow strength across domains time improve estimation precision direct survey estimators. However, introducing model assumptions carries risk model misspecification, bias, inappropriate shrinkage. address challenges, fastsae provides unified diagnostic framework centered diagnose() function dedicated S3 autoplot() visualization method. evaluates frequentist C++ EBLUP models (eblup_fh, eblup_sfh, eblup_stfh, eblup_bhf) Bayesian INLA HB models (hb_area).

title: Model Diagnostics and Residual Analysis
text: diagnostic workflow evaluates four fundamental dimensions SAE model quality: Precision Gain & RSE Reduction: Quantifies improvement Relative Standard Error (RSE=MSEθ̂×100%\text{RSE} = \frac{\sqrt{\text{MSE}}}{\hat{\theta}} \times 100\%) compared direct survey estimates. Evaluates whether areas satisfy official statistics reliability threshold (typically RSE<25%\text{RSE} < 25\% 20%20\%). Goodness--Fit Statistic (Brown et al., 2001): Computes Chi-square diagnostic statistic WW sampled domains: W=∑d=1D(yd−θ̂d)2Vd+MSE(θ̂d)W = \sum_{d=1}^D \frac{(y_d - \hat{\theta}_d)^2}{V_d + \text{MSE}(\hat{\theta}_d)} compares χ2(D)\chi^2(D). large values indicate model estimates differ direct estimates uncertainty, p-value upper-tailed (emdi). statistic ignores positive correlation ydy_d θ̂d\hat{\theta}_d, conservative: correct model WW usually well DD. Bias Diagnostic (Brown et al., 2001): regression direct estimates model estimates, yd=α+βθ̂d+ed,y_d = \alpha + \beta \hat{\theta}_d + e_d, reported descriptively (autoplot(type = "calibration")) look systematic deviations. used formal test α=0,β=1\alpha = 0, \beta = 1: shrinkage estimators EBLUP slope exceeds 1 even model correct (1/γd1/\gamma_d variation explained covariates), test reject correct models. Residual Spatial Autocorrelation (Moran’s ): Verifies whether spatial autocorrelation fully captured model random effects. Significant residual spatial clustering indicates unmodeled spatial patterns remain.

text: small areas geographic units (counties, regencies, districts), spatial correlation frequently occurs: neighboring areas tend similar outcomes distant ones. Furthermore, surveys repeated multiple years, temporal correlation time periods also present. fastsae provides specialized, high-performance implementations : 1. Spatial Fay-Herriot (eblup_sfh): Simultaneous Autoregressive SAR(1) random effects. 2. Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot (eblup_stfh): Combined spatial SAR(1) temporal AR(1) random effects.

title: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Models
text: Spatial Fay-Herriot model (Pratesi & Salvati, 2008) models area random effects using Simultaneous Autoregressive (SAR(1)) process: y=Xβ+u+ey = X\beta + u + e u=ρ1Wu+ϵ1⟹u=(−ρ1W)−1ϵ1u = \rho_1 W u + \epsilon_1 \implies u = (- \rho_1 W)^{-1} \epsilon_1 : - WW known row-standardized spatial proximity matrix (D×DD \times D). - ρ1∈(−1,1)\rho_1 \(-1, 1) spatial autoregressive parameter. - ϵ1∼N(0,σu12ID)\epsilon_1 \sim N(0, \sigma_{u1}^2 I_D) independent innovation noise. - e∼N(0,Ve)e \sim N(0, V_e) sampling error diagonal matrix Ve=diag(D1,…,DD)V_e = \text{diag}(D_1, \dots, D_D).

title: Unit-Level Estimation with Battese-Harter-Fuller
text: Unlike area-level models aggregate data prior modeling, unit-level models operate directly individual survey unit records (e.g., households, farms, persons) linking population auxiliary aggregates (e.g., census means satellite imagery). fastsae package implements nested error regression model Battese, Harter, Fuller (1988) via eblup_bhf(), providing fast estimation parallel parametric bootstrap MSE. hb_unit() fits model hierarchical Bayes model INLA (see last section).

text: individual unit jj (j=1,…,ndj = 1, \dots, n_d) small area dd (d=1,…,Dd = 1, \dots, D): ydj=xdj⊤β+ud+edjy_{dj} = x_{dj}^\top \beta + u_d + e_{dj} : - ud∼..d. N(0,σu2)u_d \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_u^2) area-specific random effect. - edj∼..d. N(0,σe2)e_{dj} \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_e^2) unit-level error variance. - udu_d edje_{dj} mutually independent. small area population mean Y‾d\bar{Y}_d estimated : Y‾̂dEBLUP=X‾d⊤β̂+γd(y‾d−x‾d⊤β̂)\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{EBLUP}} = \bar{X}_d^\top \hat{\beta} + \gamma_d (\bar{y}_d - \bar{x}_d^\top \hat{\beta}) : - X‾d\bar{X}_d known population mean vector auxiliary variables domain dd. - y‾d\bar{y}_d x‾d\bar{x}_d sample means domain dd. - γd=σu2σu2+σe2/nd\gamma_d = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2 / n_d} shrinkage ratio.

what: Understanding INLA: Fast Bayesian Inference without MCMC
title: High-Performance Frequentist and Bayesian Small Area Estimation in R
text: INLA (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations; Rue et al., 2009) provides deterministic alternative Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Bayesian inference latent Gaussian models. Instead drawing thousands samples, INLA: Approximates posterior marginals analytically using Laplace approximations Integrates non-Gaussian observations analytically Delivers results seconds rather hours fastsae uses INLA INLA R package fit hierarchical Bayesian small area models : 6 likelihood families: Gaussian, Beta, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma Spatial random effects: BYM2, Besag ICAR, Spatial Lag Temporal random effects: RW1, RW2, AR(1) Spatio-temporal interactions: separable non-separable structures Key advantage MCMC: convergence diagnostics, burn-, reproducible results, 10–100× speedups.

what: Benchmark Small Area Estimation Predictions to Aggregate Targets — benchmark_sae
title: Benchmark Small Area Estimation Predictions to Aggregate Targets — benchmark_sae
text: Calibrates small area model predictions (hb_area, eblup_fh, eblup_sfh, eblup_stfh, eblup_bhf) weighted aggregate matches known benchmark targets higher administrative levels (e.g. provincial national totals/means), required official statistics production. Supports: Single-Stage Benchmarking: Calibrates small areas directly aggregate target     (either globally within sub-regions/provinces via group). Two-Stage Hierarchical Benchmarking (Rao Molina, 2015, Sec 10.4; Steorts et al., 2014):     Calibrates small areas (e.g. 500 Kabupaten/Kota) within overarching groups (e.g. 34 Provinces)     simultaneously harmonizing provincial aggregates match overarching National Target     (national_target). Guarantees simultaneous mathematical consistency across administrative tiers:     \(\sum_{d \\text{Prov}_g} \tilde{w}_{dg} \hat{\theta}_{dg}^{\text{BM}} = T_g^*\)     \(\sum_g \tilde{W}_g T_g^* = T_{\text{nat}}\). Methods implemented: "ratio": Proportional / multiplicative adjustment. Preserves area proportions non-negativity (Rao, 2002; Rao Molina, 2015). "difference": Uniform additive adjustment (Rao Molina, 2015, Section 10.3). "optimal": Variance-weighted quadratic loss benchmarking (Datta et al., 2011; Steorts et al., 2014).     Domains higher MSE absorb larger adjustments precise domains remain minimally perturbed. "logit": Logit-scale additive shift bounded indicators \(\theta_d \(0, 1)\) (Berg Fuller, 2014).
